title: Standard smooth algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra. A *standard smooth presentation* of $A$ over $R$ consists of integers $n\ge c\ge0$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ such that the image in $A$ (under $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\alpha}A$) of the determinant $g=\det\bigl(\partial f_j/\partial x_i\bigr)_{1\le i,j\le c}$ of the $c\times c$ matrix of formal partial derivatives of $f_1,\dots,f_c$ with respect to the first $c$ variables is a unit of $A$. The integer $n-c$ is the *relative dimension* of the presentation. The $R$-algebra $A$ (or the ring map $R\to A$) is *standard smooth* if it has a standard smooth presentation.
